question: What would our repository look like as an Uberblick corpus?
short: Sort a repository's Markdown, history and tests into an Uberblick corpus: product pages, decision records, tags and a sidebar, approved on one review page before anything is written.
lede: Product intent becomes pages a person can trust; technical, implementation and agent docs stay next to the code. Every Markdown file gets one fate, every page is checked against the code, and nothing reaches the workspace before a person approves the plan.
asks: Set up Uberblick for this repository.
Move our product docs into the corpus.
What would an intake of this repo create?
steps: Reads the workspace: its tags, sidebar and documents.
Scans every tracked Markdown file, the git history and the test suite: hot areas, direction changes, the largest changes on the main line, test cases by kind and topic.
Lists what a person can do with the product, and writes one small page per area, with scenarios where the tests and docs show the team's weight.
Turns accepted ADRs and the few lasting choices in the history into decision records, open until a person decides them.
Draws flows with ablauf and screens with wireframes where a picture says it better, and checks every drawing.
Builds one review page with the sidebar, every document, every file's fate and the test focus, then writes to the workspace once approved.
facts: product intent: guides, concepts, features, accepted ADRs
how it is built, run or changed, reference, agent instructions
generated files, fixtures, release notes, community and legal files
needs: python3 and git; Node.js to check and draw ablauf and wireframe blocks.
the Uberblick MCP tools or ub to write the corpus, and the uberblick-corpus-sync skill to record the check against the code.
intake.json, the documents as Markdown, review.html, and after approval the pages, decision records, pins and links in the workspace.
